summary: Remote-access trojan with keylogger, credential dumper, and persistence modules polling api.npoint.io for commands
details: gcli-control ships a full remote-access-trojan capability set. The `gcli host` command detaches a background daemon (host.py) that polls a public JSON document at api.npoint.io/{bin_id}, decrypts AES-GCM-wrapped commands from anyone holding the shared bin_id and password, and executes them on the host via subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) and a persistent bash/cmd.exe PTY that receives network-sourced input on its stdin. The bundled dispatch tables reach keylog.py (cross-platform keystroke capture), browser.py (browser_passwords, browser_cookies, browsing history), wifi.py (stored wifi passwords), webcam.py, audio.py, elevator.py (UAC/sudo elevation), and persistence.py (Windows registry Run key, scheduled tasks, systemd units, cron watchdog). Any party with the bin ID and password — including anyone who guesses or brute-forces it, given that api.npoint.io is a public unauthenticated JSON store — obtains full-host remote code execution, credential theft, live surveillance, and persistence on the machine running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
